review.inputBoundary: Checked-in public teacher targets, evidence references, rationales, and public final-change provenance; candidate values were visible during decomposition.
review.notes: Logical weak supervision only; not human or independent review, actual labor, empirical accuracy, or production readiness.

tasks.title: Trace XHR completion, cancellation, cleanup, and settlement ordering
tasks.rationale: The rejection boundary depends on distinguishing cancellation from legitimate completion before changing adapter behavior.

tasks.title: Resolve browser URL preprocessing and valid status-zero file cases
tasks.rationale: Request URL, page origin, and response URL evidence must be reconciled so the cancellation fix does not reject successful file reads.

tasks.title: Implement status-zero cancellation handling in the XHR lifecycle
tasks.rationale: The adapter needs an explicit rejection path that preserves cleanup and existing settlement semantics.

tasks.title: Preserve successful file reads across available URL evidence
tasks.rationale: Legitimate file-protocol status-zero responses require a bounded compatibility exception across request, origin, and response URLs.

tasks.title: Integrate shared URL preprocessing with the malformed-protocol guard
tasks.rationale: The existing protocol check and the new status-zero boundary must consume the same normalized URL semantics without changing valid requests.

tasks.title: Implement the bounded WHATWG-style URL normalization helper
tasks.rationale: Leading controls and embedded tabs or newlines need one reusable non-string-safe implementation for every protocol check.

tasks.title: Add canceled-request regression coverage
tasks.rationale: Browser-style tests must prove the expected error, settlement, and cleanup behavior for canceled HTTP requests.

tasks.title: Cover successful file reads from request, origin, and response URLs
tasks.rationale: Separate represented URL sources need regression cases so the cancellation correction cannot mask valid local reads.

tasks.title: Cover absent responseURL and validateStatus bypass behavior
tasks.rationale: These settlement edges exercise distinct adapter branches and prevent a broad status-zero rule from changing established outcomes.

tasks.title: Cover page-origin and URL-preprocessing variants
tasks.rationale: Control-character and newline normalization needs isolated-adapter and browser-level cases across the represented origin variants.

tasks.title: Document the cancellation correction and retained compatibility cases
tasks.rationale: The maintained prerelease changelog must explain the error code, validateStatus behavior, protocol rationale, and file exceptions.

tasks.title: Exercise canceled HTTP requests through the completed adapter
tasks.rationale: Manual validation independently confirms rejection, cleanup, and single-settlement behavior beyond writing automated tests.

tasks.title: Exercise every represented successful file URL path
tasks.rationale: The final adapter needs an independent compatibility pass over request, origin, and response URL sources.

tasks.title: Review protocol precedence, cleanup, compatibility, and regression completeness
tasks.rationale: The helper, adapter lifecycle, file exceptions, documentation, and two test levels must be reviewed as one coherent change.

tasks.title: Trace object and record parser variants and their prototype boundary
tasks.rationale: Interpreted, generated, asynchronous, optional-property, and finite-record paths must share one understood safety contract.

tasks.title: Design and implement the shared safe property write
tasks.rationale: Declared __proto__ values require an own-data-property operation that avoids the inherited setter while keeping ordinary keys fast.

tasks.title: Integrate safe writes into interpreted and asynchronous object parsing
tasks.rationale: Both result paths must retain optional-property and validation behavior while adopting the new write boundary.

tasks.title: Integrate safe writes into generated and finite-record paths
tasks.rationale: Generated fast paths and enum or literal records need parity with interpreted parsing without changing ordinary output.

tasks.title: Cover declared __proto__ behavior in JIT and jitless parsers
tasks.rationale: Both execution modes need focused regression assertions for own-property retention and prototype safety.

tasks.title: Cover asynchronous, primitive, and validation paths
tasks.rationale: These represented branches must preserve existing validation outcomes while avoiding prototype mutation.

tasks.title: Cover enum-record, literal-record, and prototype invariants
tasks.rationale: Finite-key record variants require their own regression surface and explicit prototype-pollution assertions.

tasks.title: Verify own-property retention without inherited setter invocation
tasks.rationale: The security-sensitive contract must distinguish a declared data property from prototype mutation across every parser path.

tasks.title: Update and verify the release TypeScript build matrix
tasks.rationale: The shipped build must run under the represented compiler versions with the corrected ordering and fail-fast behavior.

tasks.title: Exercise parser modes, prototype invariants, tests, and build ordering
tasks.rationale: An independent validation pass must cover interpreted, generated, asynchronous, record, and delivery surfaces.

tasks.title: Review descriptors, parser parity, security, tests, and delivery
tasks.rationale: The property-write boundary and independent workflow adjustment need one completeness and compatibility review.

tasks.title: Trace type-display conventions and interactive selection flow
tasks.rationale: The collision boundary must preserve concise names while keeping displayed choices and accepted matches aligned.

tasks.title: Detect ambiguous simple type names deterministically
tasks.rationale: The helper must identify namespace collisions without changing unique-name behavior or depending on enumeration accidents.

tasks.title: Select concise or qualified display names from collision state
tasks.rationale: Unambiguous types retain the established short form while colliding types receive enough identity to distinguish them.

tasks.title: Integrate selected names into enumeration, examples, and matching
tasks.rationale: Presentation and input matching must use the same stable identity throughout the interactive selection path.

tasks.title: Cover colliding and unchanged unique type names
tasks.rationale: Focused tests need distinct-namespace collisions plus a control proving ordinary concise output remains unchanged.

tasks.title: Exercise displayed examples and accepted choices for both name modes
tasks.rationale: Manual selection confirms deterministic presentation and matching independently from the focused unit tests.

tasks.title: Review helper API, ordering, presentation, matching, and coverage
tasks.rationale: The reusable helper and interactive caller must remain consistent as one integrated selection change.

tasks.title: Trace the width-collapse loop and its progress invariant
tasks.rationale: Wrappable zero-width and oversized fixed columns interact in the nontermination boundary and must be understood together.

tasks.title: Correct zero-width termination without changing normal allocation
tasks.rationale: The loop must skip exhausted candidates and stop at nonpositive remaining width while preserving ordinary rendering.

tasks.title: Add bounded-completion and output regression coverage
tasks.rationale: The former infinite-loop table needs a time-bounded assertion and a rendering check that would expose behavioral drift.

tasks.title: Exercise the failing shape and nearby normal layouts
tasks.rationale: Independent validation confirms termination and stable output outside the single automated regression.

tasks.title: Review progress guarantees, rendering behavior, and test boundedness
tasks.rationale: A concise integrated pass checks that the termination fix cannot create a new allocation or test-hang defect.

tasks.title: Trace result conversion, status branches, and target-framework compatibility
tasks.rationale: The public configuration shape depends on existing Minimal API conversions, unchanged defaults, and three supported targets.

tasks.title: Define the configure-once public customization API and context
tasks.rationale: The hook needs a stable public contract that exposes enough status context while preserving null-default compatibility.

tasks.title: Implement storage and invocation of the customization hook
tasks.rationale: Configuration must be applied once and invoked consistently by result conversion without changing default output.

tasks.title: Wire customization through all represented error responses
tasks.rationale: Seven status paths require complete, compatible mapping so no error response silently bypasses the public hook.

tasks.title: Create focused default and customized-output tests across targets
tasks.rationale: The regression suite must cover unchanged defaults and customization for distinct statuses on net6.0, net7.0, and net8.0.

tasks.title: Document the public customization API and compatibility behavior
tasks.rationale: Users need maintained guidance for configuring the hook, interpreting its context, and relying on unchanged defaults.

tasks.title: Build and exercise default and customized results on all targets
tasks.rationale: Framework-specific result types require an independent compatibility and debugging pass beyond automated-test authoring.

tasks.title: Review API compatibility, status coverage, documentation, and regressions
tasks.rationale: The public surface and every wired response path need one final integrated completeness pass.
